Today I deleted my almost 2 year old account.

I am semi cord-cutting and simplifying my life, getting back to the country and living authentically.

I made a big mistake in deleting the way I did though, I cut off a new person I'd just begun chatting with. A freakin awesome person too; @rotteuxx.

It dawned on me that I could use the throwaway that I only made to contact rott, to give something back to the voat community for having spent just over 2 years hanging out here. I hope that sharing a little about my experience and ongoing recovery may help someone.

Brief Background: Just over 14 years ago I was sexually attacked by a random stranger in broad daylight and in my yard. Several neighbours were home and witnessed it. No-one came to my aid or called police. Fight or flight response kicked in and at the first chance I got I sprung up and bolted off inside and locked the door. Not one conscious thought process fired, just instinctual reaction. Real fear is a gift. The attack wasn't as bad as it could have been, not as bad as many have it but bad enough for it to have changed my life and impacted me hard.

Ultimately though, I became stronger, more resilient. I have a joy for life and everyday I am happy to be alive. Every. Day. I think I am who I am because of coming through that adversity and although I would never wish for anyone to experience it, I would wish that everyone could find the joy of living that I now have. That's what I want to share with people; living in the moment, appreciating it and not sweating the things we all stress over.

People here say 5 thank-you's, 5 things to be grateful for. I remember when I was so deep in depression that I couldn't even fathom the concept of feeling gratitude. How selfish is that? These days I couldn't imagine limiting it to 5, and they are all experience/basic needs met and people based because possessions hold no value.

Depression took me right to the brink and after I got through it I began count each day that I was here as a gift. I couldn't begin to assign a numerical value to the times I have consciously thought 'I am so glad I am here to experience this' or 'I would not have experienced that had I given in'. I had a clear moment that I will always remember when the switch flicked on and I began to appreciate life, an epiphany, but for many it just takes the hard work and good habit of being grateful for the little things throughout the day.

Anyone who is going through what I went through or something similar to what I went through; I would like to tell you that it gets better but only if you allow it to.

Once you permit yourself to feel joy it becomes easier, habitual. What starts as an epiphany or a conscious effort becomes commonplace. I get joy from the simplest things now; dew drops on the grass, the sunrise, a bird singing, anything. It's like being a kid again and it's great!

After years of floating along, procrastinating in a sense of safety because my attacker was inside, the inevitable has eventuated; he has been released this month and a new stage of growth is happening for me. I still have plenty of work to do on myself, loads of progress to make and a shit-tonne of things that I want to change about myself and things to learn.

That's what life is all about right?

That's why we are all here.

Being happy throughout the journey is what counts because no-one gets out of life alive, no-one clocks life.

Thanks for reading goatygoats, thanks for this sub and thanks @rotteuxx for showing me the way here.

Depends on how clean you want it.

Personally, I would start by burning off whatever I could, and scraping the grill while hot. After cooling, I would take both grills and all three deflectors out, and scrub them with soap and water with a wire bristle brush. While they are out, you can inspect and gently brush off the actual burners below. If you see any holes obviously plugged, you can try using a toothpick or metal skewer to unclog them (your deflectors look to be in okay shape, so likely your burner isn't clogged up).

I would use this opportunity to scrape down the insides of the BBQ as well. I wouldn't bother with soap and water for this, I would just put something under the hole in the bottom, and scrape everything down and through it. My grill has a little tray with a washable liner for catching grease there as well, which I would also clean out.

Finally, after everything has dried off and is nice and clean, I would oil the deflectors and grill. I usually just use whatever veg oil I have hanging around, and a rag. You might get a little flare up from the oil the next time you start the grill, so don't burn your eyebrows off.

It's generally a good idea to scrape down and oil the grill every time you use it, as it cleans much easier when hot, and the oil keeps the metal in excellent condition (prevents rusting, etc).

Or you can just spray it with the hose and call it a night. I'm not the boss of you.

Infrared burners are not meant to cook on low heat. Only high heat, as they vaporize the drippings when they hit the burner. Low heat will let the drippings clog it. The only time to cook on low heat is when your food is wrapped in foil tight enough to eliminate dripping, or in a pan.
